mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4% over three consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 falls >2% YoY and UNRATE >5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average by more than 3% for two consecutive months signals a strengthening manufacturing sector, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods when INDPRO is above its 12-month moving average by >3% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of less than 50,000 persons alongside a concurrent rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals labor market softening, which reduces consumer spending and corporate hiring, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when PAYEMS < 50,000 and UNRATE rises month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 6-month moving average by more than 10% signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction-related equities and reduces overall market sentiment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 6-month moving average by >10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when HOUST is below its 6-month moving average by >10% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 1% while the federal funds rate remains above 3% for three months signals a divergence between monetary policy and inflation, which creates uncertainty and volatility, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as markets anticipate policy easing.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during periods of CPIAUCSL < 1% and FEDFUNDS > 3% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% coincident with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) suggests a shift from spending to saving, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises >5% YoY and GDPC1 falls YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE < 4.5% for four consecutive months.
